column1: # l1 against default on the silesia files (one thread, archive bytes; lit = literal stream compressed / raw, tok = token streams compressed / raw)

# why: l1 takes only matches >= 32 bytes (ADR-020), so on text most bytes stay literals (dickens 99.9 %, webster 97.4 %, mozilla 88 %; nci 33 %, xml 51 %) and the literal stage - zstd frames per chunk - does the short matches with its own LZ and entropy coder; the default chain matcher takes 6-31-byte matches into the token streams, which cost more than inside zstd. l1 loses where long exact repeats dominate: nci (+3.6 %), xml (+2.0 %).
# changed between before and after: only the genome_open rows (archive bytes, encode / decode within run-to-run noise, region p50 / p99); lzbench rows identical by construction (same object code).
